claims.claim: Hong Kong should not impose a hard cap on initial rents for subdivided units.
A binding cap on initial rents would shrink the stock of subdivided units.
A hard cap would leave the most exploited tenants unprotected.
Real rent burden for SDU households worsened from 31 to 34 percent.
The 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance did not address initial rents.
The long-run elasticity of SDU-type supply to controlled rents is estimated at 0.31 to 0.48.
A 10 percent cap-induced rent reduction removes roughly 3 to 5 percent of stock over five years.
A modelled 15 percent cut in initial rents would leave 3,000 to 4,000 households per year unable to enter the segment.
The 2021 ordinance is a second-generation control, so its stability does not predict the effects of a binding initial-rent cap.
The Association's submission on landlord exit is self-interested and evidentially weak.
Berlin's Mietendeckel led to measurable supply contraction and suppressed rent increases.
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of SDU stock per year.
A band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing 40 to 60 staff-years.
Enforcement would systematically fail the most exploited tenants, such as new arrivals and those without written agreements.
61 percent of surveyed households would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year security of tenure.
The binding constraint for SDU tenants is quantity, not price.
The appropriate response is tenure security plus a light, indexed band on initial rents.
A hard cap is emotionally satisfying but economically self-defeating.
